title: Too Late To Ignore
pitch: AI is moving too fast to ignore, and too fast to catch up on later. Staying current isn't optional anymore. It's part of the job.

acts.title: The machines get capable
acts.sub: AI now writes most of the code, hands work to other AI, and is learning to act in the physical world.

acts.title: Your customers change
acts.sub: How people find, compare, buy and even befriend is moving into AI.

acts.title: Work gets rewired
acts.sub: New colleagues, new platforms, and a career ladder missing its bottom rungs.

acts.title: Follow the money
acts.sub: Trillions going in, prices moving, business models breaking, and the CFO asking for proof.

acts.title: The limits get physical
acts.sub: Power, chips, borders and regulation now decide where AI can scale.

acts.title: Trust is the new frontier
acts.sub: AI fights AI, and expertise reaches places it never reached before.

signals.title: AI Is Building the Next AI
signals.hook: Engineers increasingly steer while machines write the code, and the length of work AI can do on its own keeps doubling.
signals.why: Anyone with domain knowledge can now build working software. Customers will expect prototypes in days, not quarters.
signals.story: Vibe coding went from a 2025 joke to how real products get built. Most new builders are domain experts, not developers. The engineer is no longer the bottleneck; the idea is.

signals.title: The AI That Hires the AI
signals.hook: Agents used to need humans to connect them. Now they hand work to each other through open protocols.
signals.why: Customers' processes will increasingly run agent to agent. Whatever we sell has to be reachable by their agents, not only their people.
signals.story: Protocols like MCP and A2A let agents call tools and each other. The ambition is ahead of execution: most firms say they use agents, but only about a third of workflows are automated.

signals.title: The Robot Is Already Working at BMW
signals.hook: Humanoid robots have moved from demo videos to factory shifts, and the price is falling to car-level.
signals.why: Physical work is now in scope for AI. Customers in manufacturing, logistics and facilities will ask what this means for them.
signals.story: No sick days, no overtime. The question is shifting from whether humanoids work to which tasks pay back first.

signals.title: AI Learns the Physical World
signals.hook: Models that simulate the real world in real time are the training ground for robots, factories and digital twins.
signals.why: Industrial customers get simulation-first engineering: test a line, a warehouse or a process virtually before spending on it.
signals.story: Language models learned from text. World models learn how things move and interact. That is the missing piece for robots and digital twins.

signals.title: The Lab That Runs Itself
signals.hook: AI now designs the experiment, robots run it, and the result trains the next design, without hand-offs.
signals.why: R&D cycles that took years can compress into weeks. Customers in life sciences, materials and chemicals will reorganise R&D around it.
signals.story: Science is becoming a compute problem. The edge moves from who has the most experienced scientists to who has the fastest discovery loop.

signals.title: Your Next Customer Is an Agent
signals.hook: Shopping is starting inside AI assistants, and agents are beginning to pay on the customer's behalf.
signals.why: If an agent does the comparing, our offer has to be readable by machines: clean data, clear pricing, trusted identity.
signals.story: The friction point is trust. Some banks are blocking AI agents while US open banking rules stall. Identity and permission are the new checkout.

signals.why: Customers need help with the people side, not only the technology: skills, roles and new ways of working.
signals.story: Teams using AI together can underperform individuals using it alone. Collaboration with AI is a skill, and few leaders have it yet.

signals.title: The Bottom Rung Is Breaking
signals.hook: AI is taking the tasks juniors learned on. The evidence is contested, and that is the signal.
signals.why: If juniors don't learn by doing, who becomes the senior expert in five years? Every organisation, ours included, needs an answer.
signals.story: The clearest pattern is a tilt toward experience. Entry roles are narrowing and changing shape, not simply vanishing.

signals.why: Model choice is no longer the differentiator. Value comes from what customers build with it and how they control the cost.
signals.story: October 2026 alone brought GPT-6, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Haiku 5.5. Price per token falls; usage rises faster.

signals.why: Customers will buy outcomes they can measure. Lead with the business case, not the technology.
signals.story: The winners redesign workflows and own their data. The losers measured success by how many people opened Copilot.

signals.why: Customers want choice and no lock-in. Being model-neutral is a selling point.
signals.story: Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Apple all build their own chips. At the same time, rivals now distribute each other's models.

signals.title: AI Hits the Power Wall
signals.hook: Chips are no longer the main bottleneck. Electricity is.
signals.why: Energy and location now shape where and how fast AI scales. In Europe, grid access is a competitive factor.
signals.story: In the UK, AI build-out is being held back by grid connection queues. Tech companies are signing nuclear deals to secure supply.

signals.title: The Next Data Center Is in Your Building
signals.hook: The most valuable AI in your company may not live in someone else's cloud. It may run on your own hardware.
signals.why: Customers with sensitive data can run AI locally. Privacy and sovereignty become arguments for adoption, not against it.
signals.story: Small models on your own devices cut cost and keep data at home.

signals.story: In June, Anthropic suspended access to two frontier models to comply with US export controls, then restored it on 1 July after the controls were lifted.
